difficulty_reason: For f : X -> S locally of finite type and a short exact sequence 0 -> F' -> F -> F'' -> 0 of quasi-coherent modules, the lemma proves (1) F' and F'' relatively finitely presented imply F is, and (2) F' finite type plus F relatively finitely presented implies F'' relatively finitely presented — the extension-closure laws of the relative-presentation cone. The retained proof is written: translation into the language of schemes of the chapter's algebra theorem More on Algebra, lemma ses-relatively-finite-presentation — the affine-local dictionary (relative finite presentation of a module is exactly the finite-presentation-of-modules-over-the-relative-polynomial-presentation identity recorded by the sibling dictionary card L16180) converts the scheme statement into the ring statement verbatim, and the algebra lemma carries both clauses by the standard horseshoe/presentation-splicing argument quoted there.
